playlist.title: SSH Certificates with PKI Manager
playlist.description:
A short video series for Linux sysadmins: SSH certificate authorities from zero (episodes 1-10), then principals in depth with real-world access designs (episodes 11-19). Host and user certificates, principals, revocation (KRL), per-host blocks, zones, Ansible automation, break-glass access and CI robots, all with the open-source PKI Manager.

Companion page and diagrams: https://oriolrius.github.io/pki-manager-web/ssh/videos/
Source: https://github.com/oriolrius/pki-manager-web

videos.title: Why SSH certificates | SSH Certificates #01
videos.description:
Plain SSH keys do not scale, and "trust on first use" trusts nothing. An SSH certificate authority fixes both: every server and every laptop trusts one signer instead of every key. See what is inside a certificate and where PKI Manager fits.

Episode 01 of "SSH certificates with PKI Manager" (Series 1 · SSH certificates from zero). A short series for Linux sysadmins who know SSH but have never used an SSH certificate authority.

Chapters
0:00 Hook
0:18 Problem one: key sprawl
0:32 Problem two: trust on first use
0:47 The idea: a trusted signer
1:03 What is inside a certificate
1:17 Where PKI Manager fits

videos.title: Two CAs, trust crosses over | SSH Certificates #02
videos.description:
Every SSH login answers two questions: "is this the right server?" and "is this the right person?". So there are two CAs, a Host CA and a User CA, and their trust crosses over: the User CA key goes to the servers, the Host CA line goes to the laptops.

Episode 02 of "SSH certificates with PKI Manager" (Series 1 · SSH certificates from zero). A short series for Linux sysadmins who know SSH but have never used an SSH certificate authority.

Chapters

0:24 The Host CA
